errors.description: The derivation equates the negative log probability of an observed token with a KL divergence. These are not equal: KL is an expectation over the teacher’s token distribution, and expected negative log likelihood equals KL plus the teacher’s entropy. The displayed ratio also places `log Pπ` in the denominator. Thus Equation 6 is mathematically incorrect as written, even though the objectives can have the same minimizer under an appropriate expectation.
errors.evidence: “Σ_j -log Pπ(a_j | s, a_{<j}) = … Σ_j KL(P_teacher,j || P_π,j)”

errors.location: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, iterative sampling claim and Equation 8
errors.description: Sampling training responses from π_t does not establish that their distribution mismatch with the optimized model is reduced: training then changes the model to π_{t+1}. The manuscript gives no bound or measurement showing that this change is smaller than the mismatch it replaces, so the stated mitigation is not demonstrated by the derivation.
errors.evidence: “π_{t+1} = argmax_π … E_{a~π_t(.|s)}[r_π(s,a)]”; the text concludes that replacing π_old with π_t “effectively mitigates the distribution mismatch.”

errors.description: Choosing the best result across four temperatures for each test metric can make benchmark scores selection-biased if those same benchmark results determine the chosen temperature. The manuscript does not state that temperature selection was made independently of the evaluation benchmarks.
errors.evidence: “the model is prompted to generate responses with temperature = {0 …, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8} … For each test metric … the best result is chosen.”
